episodes.title: Introduction to Media Literacy
episodes.description: Jay introduces media literacy and the questions that help us navigate a world saturated with media.

episodes.title: History of Media Literacy, Part 1
episodes.description: Trace media literacy’s history from Ancient Greece through printing, newspapers, and yellow journalism.

episodes.title: History of Media Literacy, Part 2
episodes.description: Follow the arrival of film, television, and other screens, alongside the new approaches to media literacy they inspired.

episodes.title: Media & the Mind
episodes.description: You are constantly surrounded by media, so the question is: how does your brain handle all of that?

episodes.title: Media & Money
episodes.description: Media isn’t just movies and newspapers and TV shows, it’s also a part of society that involves a lot of money.

episodes.title: Influence & Persuasion
episodes.description: Explore how advertising persuades audiences and how it differs from public relations and propaganda.

episodes.title: Online Advertising
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Media Literacy, Jay talks about how online advertising works and why companies want to know everything you're looking at.

episodes.title: Media Ownership
episodes.description: Explore media ownership, industry mergers, and why understanding their relationships matters for media literacy.

episodes.title: Media Policy & You
episodes.description: Copyright and other media regulations have always been a bit tricky, but the internet made all of that infinitely more complicated.

episodes.title: The Dark(er) Side of Media
episodes.description: Examine propaganda, misinformation, and disinformation and why recognizing them matters for media literacy.

episodes.title: Media Skills
episodes.description: Now that you have a solid understanding of the media landscape, it’s time to equip you with the essential skills for navigating it.

episodes.title: Future Literacies
episodes.description: Consider how media literacy skills can adapt to future technologies and a changing media landscape.
